correctness.rationale: For each ell>=3, the two-digit morphism forces every four-factor difference triple into E=(1,d,1), L=(0,1,d), or R=(d,1,0). Reversal negates and reverses these triples; the images avoid their union because 1 != -1 and 0 != 1,-1 mod ell. Hence no reversed pair at length>=4. At length three any pair of occurring reversals has differences +1 and -1 and must be a palindrome. An explicit binary-position construction realizes every ordered pair, yielding all length-three factors and the exceptional short-length counts. Finite checker replays difference-class and constructive formulas, but the stated proof supplies all quantifiers.

value.rationale: It settles the explicitly posed 2024 generalized Thue-Morse reflection-complexity question for every ell>=4 and identifies an exact universal cutoff at length four, sharpening an eventual equality into an immediate local obstruction. It also classifies all low-length exceptions and palindromic length-three factors. This is an infinite family theorem for a canonical automatic-word family in combinatorics on words (68R15), not a routine finite table increment.
